target_note: WITHHELD 2026-08-30 on DEF-0190-1, the TENTH cannot-fail check found in this corpus. `audit.py`'s INERT buckets have **no detection-power conjunct**: `moved` is derived from the hash of `observed`, so an arm whose observable NEVER VARIES returns `moved = 0` BY CONSTRUCTION, and `classify()` reads that as 'the field is inert'. `INERT-MULTI` is not withheld, so such a field keeps emitter-grade status. Measured across the corpus: **8 arms record no observation at all, and 128 arms (80,138 field records) record exactly ONE distinct `observed` payload across every case.** 21 INERT-* fields rest entirely on such arms; this is one of the 5 that were emitter-grade. It is the eighth finding inverted -- there, a promotion gate could not fail; here, an INERTNESS gate cannot fail. The measurement is not refuted: the field may well be inert. But an arm that cannot vary its observable cannot establish inertness either, and that is the same error this corpus has now made ten different ways. REMEDY, needing no hardware and already IN the corpus: the `_detect`, `__ladder_L_*` and `_live_control` records -- discarded by the same underscore filter -- consumed as a GATE on INERT verdicts rather than as measurements.
